title: Before Dandadan, There Was Abenobashi: Remembering Anime's Forgotten Sleeper Hits
summary: Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi is the forgotten Gainax sleeper hit that walked so Dandadan could run. A look back at the 2002 classic, the golden age of ADV Films, and where you can still watch it.
body:
Do you remember when anime in the West felt like the Wild West? If you were watching anime in the late '90s and early 2000s, you know exactly what I'm talking about.

In 1995, Studio Gainax changed anime forever with Neon Genesis Evangelion. Five years later, the studio made FLCL, six episodes of pure chaotic craziness that became a cult classic. Then in 2002, the same studio did it again, and almost nobody remembers it.

## The grandfathers of Western anime

We owe a massive debt to the companies that brought anime to the West back then: ADV Films, Manga Entertainment and Media Blasters. They took huge risks to bring over shows nobody was sure would sell, and they built the culture we have today.

I honestly miss the presence ADV Films had in the community. Its legacy lives on through Sentai Filmworks, which grew out of ADV and still carries the torch for physical media and dubbing. But with the shift to streaming, we're slowly losing the memory of the sleeper hits from that golden era.

## Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi (2002)

Take Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi. Gainax made it in 2002 with Madhouse, and it's 13 episodes of pure chaotic energy.

Two kids from Osaka, Arumi and Sasshi, get thrown into a string of parallel worlds, and each one is a brilliant, unhinged parody of a different genre: RPGs, sci-fi epics, dating sims, film noir, kung fu cinema and more. It was scored by Shirō Sagisu, the same composer behind Evangelion, and it won an Excellence Award for animation at the Japan Media Arts Festival.

## Why it's the blueprint for Dandadan

Messy kids, reality bending around them, and slapstick comedy crashing head-first into real emotion. If that formula sounds familiar, it should. It's exactly why Dandadan is such a massive hit today.

Abenobashi was pulling off that same crazy energy more than 20 years earlier. We can't let the sleeper anime that helped build the culture we love be forgotten.

Side note: it's classic early-2000s Gainax, which means it can get a little risqué. You've been warned.

## Update (September 2026)

Good news for anybody who wants to track it down: while the physical releases are out of print, Abenobashi is streaming on HIDIVE, Sentai's streaming service. And Dandadan Season 3 is officially set for 2027 from Science Saru, so you've got time to catch up.

Sources: [HIDIVE](https://www.hidive.com/tv/magical-shopping-arcade-abenobashi), [Crunchyroll News](https://www.crunchyroll.com/news/latest/2025/12/21/dandadan-anime-season-3-2027-premiere-teaser-visual), [Wikipedia: Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magical_Shopping_Arcade_Abenobashi)

## Quick answers

What is Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi? A 13-episode 2002 anime from Gainax and Madhouse about two kids from Osaka who get thrown into parallel worlds that parody different genres.

Who made the music for Abenobashi? Shirō Sagisu, the composer behind Neon Genesis Evangelion.

Where can I watch Abenobashi? It's streaming on HIDIVE. The physical releases are out of print.

When does Dandadan Season 3 come out? In 2027. An exact date hasn't been announced yet.

Is Abenobashi like Dandadan? In spirit, yes: chaotic kids, reality-bending worlds, and comedy mixed with real emotion.

What are your favorite forgotten sleeper anime from the ADV Films era? Tell me in the comments.

title: Who's Your Daddy? Joe Jackson as a Horror Icon
summary: After watching Michael, I went down a Joe Jackson rabbit hole. Three actors, three versions, one terrifying legacy. Left, Center or Right: which Joe would you have survived?
body:
If you had to grow up with one of these Joe Jacksons, who are you picking?

I just watched Michael, immediately threw on the 1992 miniseries The Jacksons: An American Dream, and then fell straight down a rabbit hole of real Joe Jackson interviews. By the end, I had one question: why isn't Joe Jackson talked about like a horror icon?

## Why Joe Jackson belongs in the horror portal

Think about what makes a great horror villain. He's in your house. You can't escape him. He decides when the day is over. And he has a signature weapon everybody recognizes.

For the Jackson kids, that was Joe and the belt.

That's not me being dramatic. Michael and his siblings talked for years about the beatings, the fear and rehearsals that never seemed to end. Joe defended it as discipline for the rest of his life. You can argue about whether that discipline built the Jackson 5, but you can't argue that it didn't scare them.

So here's the lineup.

## Left: Colman Domingo in Michael (2026)

Cinematic dread.

This is the big-screen, prestige-movie Joe, and the fear is in the atmosphere as much as in anything he does. You find yourself watching the kids' faces as much as you watch him, because you're waiting to see what happens next.

## Center: Lawrence Hilton-Jacobs in The Jacksons: An American Dream (1992)

The Enforcer. The Belt.

If you grew up in a house that watched this miniseries, you know exactly which version I mean. Hilton-Jacobs' Joe is the one a whole generation remembers: loud, hard and dead serious about getting those boys ready. It's '90s TV-event intensity, and it stuck with people.

## Right: the real Joe Jackson

The one who actually did it.

The real Joe built the Jackson 5 out of Gary, Indiana, with a work ethic and harsh discipline he never backed away from. Watching his real interviews after two dramatized versions is a different experience. There's no score, no lighting and no actor making choices. Just a man explaining why he did it, completely convinced he was right.

That's the scariest version, because it isn't a performance.

## My pick

TBH, I'd go with Hilton-Jacobs. I'd have fewer nightmares, but I'd still end up talented and famous.

## Update (September 2026)

Two things happened after I posted this.

First, Druski. While hosting the 2026 BET Awards at the end of June, he dropped a parody trailer called "Joe," a fake prequel to Michael, with Druski in heavy makeup as Joe Jackson, belt in hand, pushing his sons to the brink. It had the internet in tears, and some people felt it went too far with Janet Jackson and Jaafar Jackson in the building. For me, it was basically in line with everything in this post: when a comedian can build a whole horror-movie trailer out of Joe Jackson and everybody instantly gets the joke, that's a horror icon.

Second, Michael turned into a monster at the box office. It opened to about $97 million in the U.S., the best opening ever for a biopic, and went on to pass $1 billion worldwide, the first biopic to get there. Lionsgate's film chief has said there's "at least one more movie," and Colman Domingo has talked about a possible part two. So we might be getting more of Domingo's Joe.

Sources: [theGrio](https://thegrio.com/2026/06/29/druski-drops-new-joe-skit-while-hosting-the-bet-awards/), [Consequence](https://consequence.net/2026/06/druski-joe-jackson-michael-biopic-parody-sketch/), [Variety](https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/michael-box-office-opening-weekend-record-1236730805/), [Screen Rant](https://screenrant.com/michael-jackson-biopic-sequel-update/)

## Quick answers

Who plays Joe Jackson in Michael? Colman Domingo, opposite Jaafar Jackson as Michael and Nia Long as Katherine Jackson.

Who played Joe Jackson in The Jacksons: An American Dream? Lawrence Hilton-Jacobs, in the 1992 miniseries.

What was Druski's Joe Jackson skit? A parody trailer called "Joe" that Druski debuted while hosting the 2026 BET Awards. It spoofs a dark prequel to Michael, with Druski playing Joe Jackson.

How much did Michael make at the box office? More than $1 billion worldwide, making it the highest-grossing biopic ever.

Is there going to be a Michael 2? Nothing's official yet, but Lionsgate's film chairman has said there's "at least one more movie."

title: Tales from the Crypt Is Back on Shudder — Do We Need a Remake?
summary: Almost 30 years after the Crypt Keeper closed the coffin, Tales from the Crypt is finally streaming on Shudder. Now the real question: do we need a remake, a reboot or a movie?
body:
Man, it's been a LONG time since I've seen the Crypt Keeper.

The last episode of Tales from the Crypt, "The Third Pig," aired back in 1996. That's almost 30 years since the show closed the coffin. And for most of that time, if you wanted to rewatch it, good luck.

Now it's finally streaming on Shudder, and I have to ask: do we need a new Tales from the Crypt?

## What made Tales from the Crypt special

Tales from the Crypt ran on HBO from 1989 to 1996: seven seasons of horror stories based on the EC Comics of the 1950s. Every episode was its own little nightmare, and most of them ended with somebody getting exactly what they deserved.

Hosting all of it was the Crypt Keeper, voiced by John Kassir: a cackling puppet corpse with a pun for everything. He was the reason you stayed for the ending. Horror comedy doesn't get much more iconic than that.

Being on HBO meant the show could go all out, too: real gore, practical effects and dark humor, with nothing cut for broadcast TV. And the guest list was ridiculous. Brad Pitt, Demi Moore, Michael J. Fox, Christopher Reeve, Kyle MacLachlan, Ewan McGregor, Steve Buscemi, Joe Pesci and Tim Curry all showed up at some point.

## Why it disappeared for so long

For years, Tales from the Crypt was one of the hardest classic horror shows to watch legally. It had never been on a streaming service. The rights were split between different companies and the people behind the original comics and the show, and nobody could get everything lined up.

That's also what killed the last attempt at bringing it back. In 2016, M. Night Shyamalan was set to revive Tales from the Crypt for TNT, and it fell apart over rights issues before it ever got made.

## Back on Shudder, uncut

Shudder started streaming Tales from the Crypt on May 1, 2026, beginning with season one and adding the rest every Friday through June 12. It's the first time the show has ever been on a streaming service, and all seven seasons are uncut and uncensored.

I'm glad it's back. A whole generation that never got to watch it on HBO can finally meet the Crypt Keeper.

## So, do we need a remake?

Here's where I'm torn.

The case for yes: anthology horror is perfect for right now. Short, nasty, standalone stories, practical effects and a host with personality. Horror fans would show up.

The case for no: the Crypt Keeper is John Kassir's voice and that specific puppet. A CGI Crypt Keeper or a gritty modern take would miss the whole point. The show worked because it was fun and mean at the same time.

If they do bring it back, keep the puppet, keep the puns and keep it R-rated. Otherwise, just let people discover the original on Shudder.

## Update (September 2026)

All seven seasons have been streaming uncut on Shudder since June 12. As of September, there's still no confirmed remake, reboot or movie.

Sources: [AMC Global Media](https://www.amcglobalmedia.com/2026/04/15/tales-from-the-crypt-streaming-for-the-first-time-exclusively-on-shudder/), [Bloody Disgusting](https://bloody-disgusting.com/tv/3949246/tales-from-the-crypt-now-streaming-for-the-very-first-time-on-shudder/), [Gizmodo](https://gizmodo.com/tales-from-the-crypt-streaming-shudder-2000745039)

## Quick answers

Where can I watch Tales from the Crypt? On Shudder. It's the first time the show has ever been available to stream, and all seven seasons are uncut.

When did Tales from the Crypt come to Shudder? Season one arrived May 1, 2026, and the rest rolled out weekly through June 12, 2026.

What was the last episode of Tales from the Crypt? "The Third Pig," which aired in 1996.

Who voices the Crypt Keeper? John Kassir.

Is there a Tales from the Crypt remake? Not as of September 2026. The last revival attempt, M. Night Shyamalan's series for TNT, fell apart over rights issues.

## Your turn

Do we need a new Tales from the Crypt? Remake, reboot or movie: yeah or nah? Tell me in the comments.

title: Not Every Book of the Dead Is the Same Kind of Curse
summary: Some guide the dead. Some weaponize the dead. Some reveal truths that break the mind. I split horror's Books of the Dead into 3 lanes. Which one is truly the worst?
body:
Not every Book of the Dead is the same kind of curse.

Some guide the dead. Some weaponize the dead. Some reveal truths that break the mind.

Horror keeps coming back to the same idea, an ancient book you should never open, but the books themselves are doing completely different jobs. So I split them into three lanes:

1. The Sacred Guide
2. Flesh-Bound Evil
3. Forbidden Cosmic Text

## Lane 1: The Sacred Guide

This is the one that's real. The ancient Egyptian Book of the Dead was never one single book. It was a collection of spells and instructions buried with the dead to help them make it through the afterlife. Its most famous moment is the weighing of the heart: your heart goes on a scale against the feather of Ma'at, and if it's heavy with wrongdoing, it gets devoured.

It was never meant to be a weapon. It's a map for the soul.

Horror still can't leave it alone, though. Movies like The Mummy turn it into something that brings the dead back instead of guiding them, because nothing's scarier than a sacred thing used wrong.

## Lane 2: Flesh-Bound Evil

This is the Evil Dead book: the Necronomicon Ex-Mortis, bound in human flesh and inked in blood. You read from it out loud, and you're not guiding the dead anywhere. You're inviting them into the living.

What comes next is possession. People you love turn into Deadites and taunt you in their own voices. It's direct, it's physical, and it happens right in front of you.

## Lane 3: Forbidden Cosmic Text

This is H.P. Lovecraft's Necronomicon, written by the "Mad Arab" Abdul Alhazred. It doesn't summon one demon to your cabin. It shows you the truth about the universe: ancient, uncaring cosmic beings, and how little humans matter to any of it.

Reading it doesn't possess your body. It breaks your mind. In Lovecraft's world, knowledge itself is the monster.

## Which one is the worst?

For me, Book 2 is the most instantly terrifying, because possession horror is direct. There's no confusion about what's happening. Something is inside the people around you, and it wants you.

But Book 3 might be worse long-term, because it's not just attacking your body. It's attacking your understanding of reality. You can fight a Deadite with a chainsaw. You can't un-learn what the Necronomicon tells you.

Book 1 is the only one I'd actually want to own. It's the only one designed to help you.

## Update (September 2026)

Lane 2 got bigger this summer. Evil Dead Burn came out in July, and this time the evil was already in the family's house: the Prices' grandfather, Benjamin, had been researching the Deadites and the Kandarian Dagger. And Evil Dead Wrath, a prequel set in 1972, is coming April 7, 2028.

For the full breakdown, read my [Evil Dead Burn review](articles/horror-evil-dead-burn-review-this-one-hits-different-and-not-how-yo.html) and [how the Burn leaks held up](articles/horror-evil-dead-burn-eyes.html).

Sources: [Wikipedia: Evil Dead Burn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evil_Dead_Burn), [Deadline on Evil Dead Wrath](https://deadline.com/2026/06/evil-dead-wrath-is-prequel-1236958743/)

## Quick answers

What is the Book of the Dead? The name covers a few very different books. The real Egyptian Book of the Dead was a collection of spells to guide the dead through the afterlife. In horror, it usually means the Evil Dead book or H.P. Lovecraft's Necronomicon.

Is the Necronomicon real? Not as an ancient book. Lovecraft invented it for his stories, and the Evil Dead movies created their own version.

What is the book in Evil Dead called? The Necronomicon Ex-Mortis, a book bound in human flesh and inked in blood.

What's the difference between Lovecraft's Necronomicon and the Evil Dead book? The Evil Dead book summons demons that possess people. Lovecraft's reveals cosmic truths that drive its readers insane.

## Your turn

Which Book of the Dead is the worst: the Sacred Guide, Flesh-Bound Evil or the Forbidden Cosmic Text? Tell me in the comments.

title: The Nightmare on Elm Street Mandela Effect Nobody Spotted
summary: For years I was sure Cathy Dennis's "Touch Me (All Night Long)" was in A Nightmare on Elm Street 2: Freddy's Revenge. It wasn't. The movie came out in 1985, and her version didn't exist until 1991. Turns out I created my own Mandela effect.
body:
For years, I was convinced Cathy Dennis's "Touch Me (All Night Long)" was in A Nightmare on Elm Street Part 2: Freddy's Revenge. I would've bet money on it.

I was wrong. And the way I got it wrong is kind of fascinating.

## How my brain rewrote a horror movie

I saw Freddy's Revenge as a kid once or twice, then didn't watch it again until the early 2000s. In between, I heard Cathy Dennis's version of "Touch Me (All Night Long)" so many times that my brain quietly stitched the two memories together.

So when I finally rewatched the movie, the song didn't sound like the version in my head. I was like, "What in the dream warrior is this?"

## The timeline doesn't lie

The dates make it impossible:

- Freddy's Revenge came out in 1985.
- Cathy Dennis's version came out in 1991.

The song in the movie is the original "Touch Me (All Night Long)" by Wish featuring Fonda Rae, from 1984. It's the track Jesse dances to in that famous scene where he's unpacking and cleaning up his room. Cathy Dennis's cover came six years after the movie.

My memory didn't just fade. It swapped in a recording that didn't even exist yet.

## Two versions, two different vibes

Both versions are bangers, but they don't have the same energy.

The Wish and Fonda Rae original is mid-'80s club music: synth-heavy, with Fonda Rae's big vocal out front. It reached number 5 on Billboard's dance club chart and number 49 in the UK.

Cathy Dennis's version is glossy early-'90s dance-pop, and it was a much bigger hit. It went to number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in May 1991 and number 1 on the dance club chart. That's the version that was all over the radio, which is exactly why it overwrote the original in my head.

## So is it really a Mandela effect?

A Mandela effect is usually a false memory that a lot of people share. I can't prove this one is widespread, which is why I'm asking. But on a personal level, it's the same thing: a confident memory built out of two different sources.

And it makes sense that it happened with this movie. Freddy's Revenge is the odd one out in the Nightmare series, and that dance scene is one of the most talked-about moments in it. A scene that memorable, paired with a song that later became a bigger hit in a different version, is the perfect setup for your brain to mix things up.

## Update (September 2026)

Freddy's coming back. In July, Paramount announced a new A Nightmare on Elm Street movie after making a deal with Wes Craven's estate for the U.S. rights. It's based on the original 1984 film and comes from Paramount Primal, the studio's new horror label run by J.D. Lifshitz and Raphael Margules, the producing team behind Barbarian and Weapons. Craven's widow, Iya Labunka, and his son, Jonathan Craven, are producing. There's no release date yet.

Sources: [Variety](https://variety.com/2026/film/news/nightmare-on-elm-street-reboot-paramount-wes-craven-estate-1236809749/), [The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/nightmare-on-elm-street-movie-paramount-1236646496/), [Wikipedia: Touch Me (All Night Long)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touch_Me_(All_Night_Long))

## Quick answers

What song is in A Nightmare on Elm Street 2: Freddy's Revenge? "Touch Me (All Night Long)" by Wish featuring Fonda Rae, the 1984 original, plays in the scene where Jesse dances while cleaning up his room.

Is Cathy Dennis's "Touch Me (All Night Long)" in Freddy's Revenge? No. Her cover came out in 1991, six years after the movie.

When did Freddy's Revenge come out? In 1985.

How high did Cathy Dennis's "Touch Me" chart? It reached number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in May 1991.

Is there a new Nightmare on Elm Street movie? Yes. Paramount announced one in July 2026, based on the 1984 original, but there's no release date yet.

## Your turn

Which version sounds right to you: Wish and Fonda Rae, or Cathy Dennis? And be honest: does the Cathy Dennis version feel more right than the original? Drop your answer in the comments.

title: XFD's Mount Rushmore of Legends: Romero, Toriyama, Hulk Hogan, Steve Jobs
summary: Horror: George Romero. Anime: Akira Toriyama. Wrestling: Hulk Hogan. Tech: Steve Jobs. I made the call. Now tell me who doesn't belong.
body:
I finally made my Mount Rushmore, and I already know somebody's getting replaced in the comments.

- Horror: George A. Romero
- Anime: Akira Toriyama
- Wrestling: Hulk Hogan
- Tech: Steve Jobs

My rule was simple: each one had to change their category in a major way. Not just be great at it. Change it.

## Horror: George A. Romero

Before Night of the Living Dead in 1968, movie zombies were mostly voodoo zombies, people under a spell. Romero turned them into the slow, hungry, flesh-eating dead that just keep coming, and every zombie movie, show and game since is standing on that.

He didn't stop there. Dawn of the Dead turned a shopping mall into a statement about consumerism, and Day of the Dead kept pushing. Romero used zombies to talk about society, and horror has been doing it ever since.

If you've watched The Walking Dead, played Resident Evil or seen any zombie movie at all, you've seen Romero's influence.

## Anime: Akira Toriyama

Dragon Ball changed everything. Goku became the blueprint for the shonen hero, and a huge part of the anime and manga that came after, from Naruto to One Piece, grew up in his shadow.

And Toriyama wasn't just Dragon Ball. He created Dr. Slump, and he designed the characters and monsters for Dragon Quest and the characters for Chrono Trigger, so his art shaped video games, too.

He passed in March 2024, and the whole world felt it.

## Wrestling: Hulk Hogan

Hulkamania took wrestling from a regional business to pop culture. Hogan main-evented the first WrestleMania, slammed André the Giant at WrestleMania III and became the face of the WWF boom in the '80s. Then he turned heel, joined the nWo in 1996 and helped WCW take over Monday nights.

Hogan is also the pick I expect the most heat on. Between the controversies later in his life and names like Stone Cold Steve Austin and The Rock, there's a real argument. But in terms of changing the category, the '80s boom doesn't happen without him. He died in July 2025.

## Tech: Steve Jobs

Apple, the Mac, the iPod, the iPhone. Jobs changed how normal people use technology, and then changed it again. The iPhone alone reshaped how everybody lives.

Bonus fact: Jobs bought the computer graphics group that became Pixar, and Pixar made Toy Story, the first fully computer-animated feature film. (If you read [my Toy Story 5 theory](articles/popculture-toy-story-5-is-actually-a-reboot-sequel.html), you know ReBoot got there first on TV.)

## Why these four

All four took something that already existed and changed what it meant. Romero redefined zombies. Toriyama redefined the shonen hero. Hogan made wrestling mainstream entertainment. Jobs made computers personal and phones essential.

But I know this list won't be safe.

## Update (September 2026)

These legacies are still making news:

- Romero: Twilight of the Dead, the long-planned final chapter of his zombie saga, is moving forward with Kate Beckinsale starring, the Paz brothers directing and the Romero estate on board.
- Toriyama: Dragon Ball Super is starting over this fall as Dragon Ball Super: Beerus, an enhanced version of the anime. He also worked on Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 before he passed.
- Hogan: A biopic is back on the table. His son, Nick Hogan, said in April there's "absolutely potential" for a movie, after the earlier Netflix project with Chris Hemsworth and director Todd Phillips was dropped.

Sources: [Deadline](https://deadline.com/2026/05/kate-beckinsale-twilight-of-the-dead-movie-romero-1236904663/), [Dragon Ball official site](https://en.dragon-ball-official.com/news/01_3976.html), [Push Square](https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2026/04/akira-toriyama-worked-on-ps5s-dragon-ball-xenoverse-3-before-his-passing), [Fightful](https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/nick-hogan-says-hulk-hogan-biopic-is-still-possible/)

## Quick answers

Who is on XFD's Mount Rushmore? George A. Romero for horror, Akira Toriyama for anime, Hulk Hogan for wrestling and Steve Jobs for tech.

Why is George Romero so important to horror? His 1968 film Night of the Living Dead created the modern flesh-eating zombie that nearly every zombie story since has built on.

What did Akira Toriyama create? Dragon Ball and Dr. Slump, plus the character designs for Dragon Quest and Chrono Trigger.

Did Steve Jobs have anything to do with Toy Story? Yes. Jobs bought the computer graphics group that became Pixar, the studio that made Toy Story.

## Your turn

Who does NOT belong? And who would you put up there instead? Tell me in the comments.

title: Jade Cargill's Live TV Moment: Wardrobe Fail or Elite Recovery?
summary: Jade Cargill's wig came off mid-match on live SmackDown, and she kept moving like a final boss. Wardrobe fail or elite recovery? And who gets MVP: Jade, the stylist, the glue or the referee?
body:
Jade Cargill had a live TV situation happening in real time, and she still stayed in character, kept moving and made it through the sequence.

She was out there fighting for her life, y'all.

## What happened

It was the June 12 episode of SmackDown, in a Queen of the Ring fatal four-way against Charlotte Flair, Lyra Valkyria and Sol Ruca. Jade climbed to the top rope, Charlotte joined her on the turnbuckle, Sol Ruca came in underneath, and the two of them brought Jade crashing down with a superplex.

The impact pulled Jade's wig right off, live on TV.

## The recovery

This is the part that matters. Jade didn't freeze and she didn't break character. She rolled out of the ring, fixed what she could, got back in and kept working the match. Charlotte ended up winning by making Lyra tap out to the Figure Eight, but the moment everybody was talking about was Jade.

So the real debate is this: was it a wardrobe and hair fail, or was it actually an elite recovery under pressure? 🤔

## Who gets MVP?

The nominees:

- Jade, for staying in it on live TV.
- The stylist.
- The glue.
- The referee, trying to save the whole situation.

title: Where Did Your Xeno Story Start? XFD's JRPG Origin
summary: Mine was Xenosaga, in the middle of my whole Neon Genesis Evangelion phase. Xenogears, Xenosaga, Xenoblade: where did YOUR Xeno story begin?
body:
Where did your Xeno story actually begin?

Mine was Xenosaga. I was going through my whole Neon Genesis Evangelion phase and loved my JRPGs back in those days, and Xenosaga felt like it was made for exactly that version of me.

If you're new to the series, here's the whole Xeno line:

Xenogears (1998) → Xenosaga (2002) → Xenoblade Chronicles (2010 and beyond)

## Xenogears (1998)

It started at Square, on the original PlayStation. Director Tetsuya Takahashi made Xenogears: giant robots called Gears, religion, philosophy, memory and identity, all packed into one enormous RPG. It was so ambitious that its second disc famously tells a lot of the story through narration, because the team ran out of time to build it all.

## Xenosaga (2002–2006)

After Xenogears, Takahashi co-founded Monolith Soft, and the studio made Xenosaga for Namco on the PS2. It came out as a trilogy: Episode I in 2002 in Japan (2003 in North America), Episode II in 2004 and Episode III in 2006.

It was big, cinematic science fiction, with Nietzsche in the subtitles, Gnostic ideas all over the story, KOS-MOS and Shion Uzuki at the center, and cutscenes long enough to watch like a movie.

## Why it clicked with Evangelion fans

If you were deep into Evangelion, Xenosaga felt like the game version of that headspace. Both lean hard on religious symbolism, giant weapons with mysterious origins, and characters whose minds are as much of a battlefield as any fight. That's exactly where I was at the time.

## Xenoblade Chronicles (2010–present)

Nintendo bought Monolith Soft in 2007, and in 2010 the studio launched Xenoblade Chronicles on the Wii (2012 in North America). The series kept growing: Xenoblade Chronicles X on the Wii U (2015), Xenoblade Chronicles 2 (2017) and 3 (2022) on the Switch, plus Definitive Editions of the first game (2020) and X (2025).

Giant open worlds, sometimes on the bodies of dead titans, and some of the best music in any RPG. For a lot of younger fans, this is where their Xeno story starts.

## Quick answers

What order do the Xeno games come in? Xenogears (1998), Xenosaga Episodes I–III (2002–2006), then Xenoblade Chronicles (2010), Xenoblade Chronicles X (2015), Xenoblade Chronicles 2 (2017) and Xenoblade Chronicles 3 (2022).

Are Xenogears, Xenosaga and Xenoblade connected? Not directly. They share creator Tetsuya Takahashi and a lot of themes, but they're separate stories.

Who made Xenosaga? Monolith Soft, with Namco publishing it on the PS2.

Is Xenosaga on modern consoles? No. The trilogy has never been remastered or re-released beyond the PS2, aside from a Japan-only retelling on the Nintendo DS.

title: Nintendo Is Staying Cautious on AI — and That Might Be the Smarter Move
summary: While other companies rush into generative AI, Nintendo seems focused on protecting its IP, its game quality and its fans' trust. Here's why staying cautious might be its biggest advantage.
body:
Is Nintendo being smart by staying cautious with generative AI, or is it falling behind?

While other companies rush into AI, Nintendo seems focused on protecting three things:

1. Copyright and IP
2. Game quality
3. Fan trust

## Why Nintendo has more to lose than anybody

Nintendo's brand is built on polish and that "Nintendo magic." Mario, Zelda and Pokémon aren't just games. They're some of the most valuable characters in the world. So generative AI hits Nintendo from two directions.

First, protection. AI tools trained on the internet can spit out Nintendo-looking characters in seconds, and Nintendo has spent decades defending its IP harder than almost anyone.

Second, quality. Nintendo's reputation is that its games feel handmade and finished. If AI makes games feel cheap, risky or soulless, that damages the one thing Nintendo can't afford to lose.

## Cautious isn't the same as anti-AI

I don't think Nintendo is anti-AI. I think it's being careful.

Games have used "AI" for decades: enemy behavior, pathfinding, how characters move around a level. That's not what people are arguing about. The debate is about generative AI: art, voices, writing and code made by models.

Nintendo can let everybody else find the problems first, then use whatever actually works.

## Fan trust is the real currency

Gamers are quick to call out AI-generated art, voices and assets, and the backlash can overshadow an entire game. Nintendo fans trust that a Nintendo game was made with care. Staying cautious protects that trust, and that's worth more than whatever time AI might save.

## Update (September 2026)

Nintendo's own words back this up. President Shuntaro Furukawa has said generative AI "can be used in creative ways" but that video games "cannot be created by technology alone," and that Nintendo will protect its intellectual property as AI laws develop around the world. This summer, Nintendo made it clear again that it will go after IP infringement whether AI is involved or not.

Not anti-AI. Careful. Exactly what I thought.

Sources: [Game Developer](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/nintendo-president-says-generative-ai-can-be-used-in-creative-ways-), [AUTOMATON](https://automaton-media.com/en/news/nintendo-did-not-say-they-wont-use-gen-ai-in-first-party-games-but-heres-what-they-did-say/), [Nintendo Life](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2026/07/nintendo-will-remain-tough-on-ip-infringement-whether-ai-is-used-or-not)

## Quick answers

Does Nintendo use generative AI in its games? Nintendo hasn't said it does. President Shuntaro Furukawa has said the technology "can be used in creative ways," but that games "cannot be created by technology alone."

What is Nintendo's stance on AI? Open but careful: it's willing to consider creative uses, and it's focused on protecting its intellectual property as AI laws develop.

Has Nintendo used AI in games before? Yes, in the traditional sense, like systems that control how enemy characters move.

## Your turn

title: New to Apple. But Not New to Tech. iOS 27's 'New' Features Already Existed
summary: iOS 27's 'new' features: Google did most of them back in 2017, and Splitwise did one in 2011. I made the receipts. Which one feels most 'finally' to you?
body:
NEW TO APPLE. BUT NOT NEW TO TECH.

When Apple showed off iOS 27 at WWDC in June, a few of the "new" features looked very familiar. So I made the receipts. Google did most of them back in 2017. Splitwise did one in 2011.

## 1. Visual AI: point, scan, ask

Apple: Siri in the camera. Point your iPhone at something, scan it and ask about it.

Before Apple: Google Lens, which launched on the Pixel 2 on October 19, 2017.

Useful? Absolutely. But it's about eight years late. Smart, or just familiar?

## 2. Bill splitting

Apple: point Siri at a receipt, and it can pick out the items and split the bill with your friends using Apple Cash.

Before Apple: Splitwise, which launched on August 1, 2011.

I've used Splitwise since my college days. Convenient, or just late?

## 3. Parental controls

Apple: a redesigned Screen Time, with Time Allowances (daily limits by app category, with suggestions based on your kid's age), Schedules for when apps are available, weekly usage summaries and Ask to Browse, so kids can request websites that aren't approved yet.

Before Apple: Google Family Link, from March 2017, which already let parents set daily limits, bedtimes and app approvals.

## Why this keeps happening

Apple is rarely first, and it doesn't try to be. It waits, watches what works, then builds a polished version right into the iPhone and presents it like it's brand new. For people who are new to Apple, it really is new. For everybody else, it's a feature we've been using for years, just with better marketing.

That's not all bad. Built-in usually means easier. But "new" and "new to Apple" aren't the same thing.

## Update (September 2026)

iOS 27 is out now. Apple released it on September 14. A couple of corrections to my original post: Apple's name for the camera feature is Siri Mode (it's a rebrand of Visual Intelligence), not "Siri Camera," and the bill splitting runs through Siri Mode and Apple Cash. The parental controls aren't called "Family Dashboard" either: it's a redesigned Screen Time with Time Allowances, Schedules and Ask to Browse, and it needs every device in your Family Sharing group updated to the new versions.

Sources: [MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/14/apple-releases-ios-27/), [9to5Mac on the Screen Time changes](https://9to5mac.com/2026/09/14/heres-whats-new-with-parental-control-features-in-ios-27-ipados-27-and-macos-27/), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/08/apple-is-fixing-the-headache-of-splitting-the-bill-with-its-new-siri-in-camera-feature/), [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/phones/iphones/ios-27-is-official-all-the-new-upgrades-and-features-announced-at-wwdc-2026)

## Quick answers

When did iOS 27 come out? September 14, 2026.

What is Siri Mode in iOS 27? The new name for Apple's Visual Intelligence camera feature: point your camera at something and ask Siri about it. It can also read receipts and split bills with Apple Cash.

Did Google Lens come before Apple's camera AI? Yes. Google Lens launched on the Pixel 2 in October 2017.

When did Splitwise launch? In 2011.

What's new in Screen Time in iOS 27? A redesign with Time Allowances for daily limits by app category, Schedules, weekly usage summaries and Ask to Browse for website requests.

title: Apple Just Raised Prices Across Its Entire Lineup — Here's the Real Reason Why
summary: Apple raised prices across Macs, iPads, Apple TV, HomePod and Vision Pro, and Apple TV jumped 54%. The reason: AI data centers are buying up the memory chips everything else needs.
body:
Apple just raised the price of Apple TV by 54%. That's the biggest percentage jump of anything they sell.

On June 25, Apple raised prices on 14 products at once: every Mac, every iPad, Apple TV, both HomePods and Vision Pro. Apple actually held off for months before finally doing it.

## The full list

Starting prices in the U.S., before and after, biggest jump first:

- Apple TV: $129 → $199 (+54%)
- Mac mini (256GB): $599 → $799 (+33%)
- Mac Studio (M3 Ultra): $3,999 → $5,299 (+33%)
- HomePod mini: $99 → $129 (+30%)
- iPad: $349 → $449 (+29%)
- iPad Air: $599 → $749 (+25%)
- Mac Studio (M4 Max): $1,999 → $2,499 (+25%)
- iPad mini: $499 → $599 (+20%)
- iPad Pro: $999 → $1,199 (+20%)
- MacBook Air: $1,099 → $1,299 (+18%)
- MacBook Pro: $1,699 → $1,999 (+18%)
- HomePod: $299 → $349 (+17%)
- MacBook Neo: $599 → $699 (+17%)
- iMac: $1,299 → $1,499 (+15%)
- Mac mini (M4 Pro): $1,399 → $1,599 (+14%)
- Vision Pro: $3,499 → $3,699 (+6%)

What didn't change in June: iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods, Studio Display and accessories like the Apple Pencil.

## Why it's happening

AI companies are buying up the memory chips (RAM and storage) that go into phones and laptops to fill their data centers. That's left less supply for regular companies like Apple, Dell and Microsoft, and memory prices shot up. Tim Cook called the demand a "100-year flood" and said the increases were unavoidable.

The products that need the most memory, like Macs and iPads, took the biggest hits. The ones that need less, like Apple Watch and AirPods, didn't move.

## Update (September 2026)

It reached the iPhone. At Apple's September 9 event, the iPhone Air went up to $1,099 and the iPhone 17e to $699, $100 more each.

One correction from my original post: I listed the MacBook Air as starting at $1,000 and the MacBook Pro at $1,600. The old starting prices were $1,099 and $1,699. The percentages I posted were right.

Sources: [MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/06/25/apple-just-increased-prices/), [9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/17/apple-confirms-price-increases-are-coming-to-its-products-due-to-ram-shortage/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/19/memory-crisis-hits-such-extremes-that-even-apple-cant-be-safe-.html), [Wikipedia: iPhone Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_Air), [Wikipedia: iPhone 17e](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_17e)

## Quick answers

Why did Apple raise prices in 2026? Because of a memory chip shortage, as AI data centers buy up the RAM and storage chips that computers and phones need.

When did Apple raise prices? On June 25, 2026, for Macs, iPads, Apple TV, HomePod and Vision Pro.

How much is the Apple TV now? $199, up from $129.

Did iPhone prices go up? Not in June. In September, Apple raised the iPhone Air to $1,099 and the iPhone 17e to $699.

summary: Your favorite '90s game might reveal your toxic trait. Mario 64 avoids structure, Zelda turns pain into lore, Sonic 2 rushes everything, NiGHTS lives in delusion, Street Fighter II argues to win, Pokémon keeps backup options and Resident Evil fears losing control.
body:
Your favorite '90s game might be your red flag. Be honest:

- Super Mario 64 avoids structure.
- Zelda turns pain into lore.
- Sonic 2 rushes everything.
- NiGHTS lives in delusion.
- Street Fighter II argues to win.
- Pokémon keeps backup options.
- Resident Evil fears losing control.

Here's the breakdown.

## Super Mario 64: avoids structure

Mario 64 (1996) was the first great 3D playground. You could chase Power Stars in almost any order, skip whole chunks of the castle and just run around the courtyard doing backflips. Mario 64 people see a to-do list and go explore the castle instead.

## Zelda: turns pain into lore

Zelda fans don't have trauma. They have a timeline. Every sad moment, every ruined kingdom and every "what happened here?" becomes a theory. Whether you grew up on A Link to the Past or Ocarina of Time, you know somebody who can explain the timeline split better than their own feelings.

## Sonic 2: rushes everything

Gotta go fast. Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (1992) was built for speed, and Sonic 2 people bring that energy everywhere: skipping instructions, skimming texts and speedrunning conversations. Spin dash first, ask questions later.

## NiGHTS into Dreams: lives in delusion

NiGHTS (1996) literally takes place inside dreams, and NiGHTS fans have been living there ever since. Flying through dreamscapes on the Sega Saturn? Beautiful. Still waiting on a proper modern sequel? That's the delusion.

## Street Fighter II: argues to win

If you played Street Fighter II (1991), you've argued about cheap moves, button mashing and whether a round "counts." Street Fighter II people don't lose. They get robbed.

## Pokémon: keeps backup options

Six in the party and a PC full of boxes. Pokémon Red and Blue taught a whole generation to always keep options in storage, just in case. Pokémon people never fully close a door.

## Resident Evil: fears losing control

Limited ammo. Limited saves. Tank controls and a door-opening animation that makes you hold your breath. Resident Evil (1996) trained people to hoard every herb and never waste a single bullet. Resident Evil people need to know exactly what's in the inventory at all times.

## Quick answers

What year did Super Mario 64 come out? 1996, on the Nintendo 64.

What is NiGHTS into Dreams? A 1996 Sega Saturn game from Sonic Team where you fly through dream worlds as NiGHTS.

When did Street Fighter II come out? In arcades in 1991.

When did the first Resident Evil come out? In 1996, on the PlayStation.

title: Before Gaming Got Scammed: The Nintendo Wii Era They Don't Want You to Remember
summary: The Wii launched at $249 with Wii Sports in the box. The Switch 2 launched at $449 and hit $499 in September. We're paying more for hardware, $70-plus for games and $50 a year to rent our childhood memories back. Are we moving backward?
body:
The Wii launched at $249 with Wii Sports in the box.

The Switch 2 base model launched at $449, and by September it's $499.

We're paying more for the hardware, $70 for the games and $50 a year just to rent our childhood memories back. So are we moving backward, or is this just "progress"?

## When $249 got you a whole party

When the Wii came out in 2006, $249 got you the console, a Wii Remote, a Nunchuk and Wii Sports. Plug it in, and ten minutes later your grandma was bowling. Tennis, baseball, boxing and bowling: that one disc turned living rooms into arenas.

That's why the Wii sold more than 100 million units. It wasn't the most powerful console. It was the easiest one to love.

## What that money gets you now

Here's the Switch 2 math:

- The console launched at $449.99 in June 2025.
- Big first-party games cost $70 or more. Mario Kart World launched at $79.99.
- Online play needs Nintendo Switch Online, and the Expansion Pack tier with the classic game libraries is $49.99 a year.

Some of those classic games are the same ones we already bought on the Wii's Virtual Console. Now we rent them back every year.

## "Before gaming got scammed"

I don't think everything was better back then, and I know prices go up. But something did change. Games used to be a thing you bought once. Now there's a subscription for online play, a subscription for the classics, paid "upgrades" for games you already own, and a base price that keeps climbing.

The Wii era was the last time a full-price console came with a full-price party in the box.

## Update (September 2026)

The price increase happened: on September 1, the Switch 2 went from $449.99 to $499.99 in the U.S., with increases in Europe and Canada too. Nintendo pointed to rising memory chip costs and tariffs.

Sources: [Variety](https://variety.com/2026/gaming/news/nintendo-switch-2-price-increase-20-million-sold-1236741441/)

## Quick answers

How much did the Wii cost at launch? $249.99 in the U.S., with Wii Sports included.

How much is the Switch 2? It launched at $449.99 and went up to $499.99 in the U.S. on September 1, 2026.

How much does Nintendo Switch Online cost? The Expansion Pack tier, with the classic game libraries, is $49.99 a year for an individual membership.

How many Wii consoles were sold? About 101.6 million worldwide.

title: Before MK2: Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa Built the Mortal Kombat Movie on His Shoulders
summary: As Mortal Kombat II hit theaters, I paid tribute to the man who set the standard: Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa. From Shang Tsung to The Man in the High Castle, Teen Titans and Johnny Tsunami. Rest in peace to a true legend.
body:
As the world headed to theaters for Mortal Kombat II, I wanted to take a moment to honor the man who set the standard.

Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa died in December 2025, at 75. From the 1995 tournament to his final roles, he wasn't just an actor in a video game movie. He was the soul of the tournament.

This tribute has five chapters: the villain, the actor, the artist, the mentor and the angel.

## The villain: Shang Tsung in Mortal Kombat (1995)

"Your soul is mine."

Nobody says it like him. The 1995 Mortal Kombat worked because Tagawa played Shang Tsung like he was in a real epic, not a video game movie. He was elegant, cruel and completely in control, and he looked like he was having the time of his life. A villain like that makes the heroes matter.

Years later, he came back to the role one more time, voicing Shang Tsung and lending him his likeness in the Mortal Kombat 11 video game.

## The actor: The Man in the High Castle

A lot of people only knew him as Shang Tsung until The Man in the High Castle. In Amazon's alternate-history series, where the Axis powers won World War II, he played Nobusuke Tagomi, the Japanese Trade Minister in San Francisco: a quiet, thoughtful man trying to hold onto his conscience inside a brutal system. It's one of the best performances of his career.

## The artist: Teen Titans: Trouble in Tokyo

In the 2006 movie Teen Titans: Trouble in Tokyo, Tagawa voiced Brushogun, an artist trapped inside a cursed printing press that uses his powers against his will to create criminals. It's a sad, strange role, and his voice gives it real weight.

## The mentor: Johnny Tsunami

For a lot of Disney Channel kids, he was Johnny's grandfather, the surfing legend in Johnny Tsunami (1999). "I'm proud of you, son." Warm, funny and wise, and about as far from Shang Tsung as you can get. That's how much range he had.

## The angel

The tribute ends with a digital art reveal in his honor. Rest in peace to a true legend.

## Why he set the standard

Video game movies had a rough reputation in the '90s, and plenty of them earned it. Tagawa is a big reason Mortal Kombat is remembered differently. He took the role seriously, and that let the audience take it seriously too. Every Shang Tsung since has been measured against him.

## Update (September 2026)

Mortal Kombat II opened on May 8 with about $38.5 million in the U.S. and finished around $129 million worldwide, on a reported $80 million budget.

Sources: [Deadline](https://deadline.com/2025/12/cary-hiroyuki-tagawa-dead-mortal-kombat-actor-1236636368/), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2025/12/05/entertainment/cary-hiroyuki-tagawa-dies-obit-hnk), [Wikipedia: Mortal Kombat II (film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortal_Kombat_II_(film))

## Quick answers

Who played Shang Tsung in the 1995 Mortal Kombat movie? Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa.

When did Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa die? On December 4, 2025, at 75, from complications of a stroke.

Who did Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa play in The Man in the High Castle? Nobusuke Tagomi, the Japanese Trade Minister.

Was Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa in Johnny Tsunami? Yes. He played Johnny's grandfather in the 1999 Disney Channel movie.

When did Mortal Kombat II come out? May 8, 2026.

title: How Nostalgia Quietly Rewrites the Pop Culture We Grew Up On
summary: Movies, music and memes blur together until we remember a version of the past that never aired. Here's why pop culture nostalgia keeps inventing Mandela effects, including one I accidentally made myself.
body:
Pop culture is the easiest place to catch your own brain lying to you.

A song you swear was in a movie. A logo you'd bet money looked different. A line everybody quotes that was never actually said. The more a moment gets replayed, remixed and meme-ified, the further it drifts from what really happened.

## Nostalgia doesn't store the past. It re-renders it.

That's the engine behind every Mandela effect. Your brain doesn't keep a perfect recording of a movie you saw in 1995. Every time you remember it, you rebuild it, and every rebuild pulls in whatever else is floating around: other movies, songs you heard later, jokes, memes and the way people talk about it now.

Do that enough times, and the memory stops being a record and turns into a remix.

## The classics everybody gets wrong

Some of the most famous examples:

- "Luke, I am your father." Darth Vader actually says, "No, I am your father."
- The Berenstain Bears. It's "Berenstain," not "Berenstein," no matter how many people remember the "-stein."
- The Monopoly man's monocle. He doesn't have one.
- "Mirror, mirror on the wall." In Disney's Snow White, the Queen says, "Magic mirror on the wall."
- Shazaam, the '90s genie movie starring Sinbad that tons of people remember watching. It doesn't exist.

## I did it to myself

I found out the hard way. For years, I was sure Cathy Dennis's "Touch Me (All Night Long)" was in A Nightmare on Elm Street 2. It wasn't. The movie came out in 1985, and her version didn't exist until 1991. My brain mixed a song I heard on the radio a thousand times into a movie I saw once as a kid. I broke it all down in [my Nightmare on Elm Street Mandela effect](articles/horror-nightmare-elm-street-mandela.html).

## Studios know exactly how this works

Half of modern reboots are selling you the feeling of a memory, not the thing itself. That's why [the new CGI Barney](articles/horror-practical-effects.html) feels off to people who grew up with the suit, and why [turning Martin into a gritty drama](articles/horror-modern-drama-remake.html) sounds so wrong. The memory is the product. When a reboot doesn't match the version in your head, it feels like something was taken from you.

That's the lane the Pop Culture portal lives in: movies, music, celebrities, trends and the shared moments everybody remembers slightly wrong.

## Quick answers

What is the Mandela effect? When a lot of people share the same false memory, like remembering the Berenstain Bears as the "Berenstein" Bears.

Why is it called the Mandela effect? The name comes from people who remembered Nelson Mandela dying in prison in the 1980s. He was actually released in 1990 and later became president of South Africa.

Why does nostalgia change our memories? Memories get rebuilt every time we recall them, so things we see and hear later can blend into the original.

What does Darth Vader actually say? "No, I am your father." Not "Luke, I am your father."

title: The Incomparable Roberta Flack 🎤✨ #RobertaFlack #SoulMusic #Shorts
summary: A tribute to the incomparable Roberta Flack: "Killing Me Softly," "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" and "Tonight, I Celebrate My Love." The soul legend's voice will outlive us all. What's your favorite song of hers?
body:
Some voices don't need to be loud to stop a room. Roberta Flack's was one of them.

In this short, I put together a few timeless moments from the legendary Roberta Flack: "Killing Me Softly with His Song," "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" and "Tonight, I Celebrate My Love." One minute isn't close to enough, but it's a start.

## The voice

Roberta Flack could make a song feel like a private conversation. She didn't oversing. She slowed things down, held back and let every word land, and somehow that hit harder than any big note.

She was a trained musician, too. She started out as a classical piano prodigy, earned a music scholarship to Howard University at 15, and taught music before her career took off. You can hear that control in everything she recorded.

## Back-to-back Record of the Year

Here's a stat that still sounds made up: Roberta Flack was the first artist to win the Grammy for Record of the Year two years in a row.

- "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" won in 1973. The song got a second life after Clint Eastwood used it in Play Misty for Me.
- "Killing Me Softly with His Song" won in 1974.

## The songs in this tribute

"Killing Me Softly with His Song" is the one everybody knows, and a whole new generation found it through the Fugees' 1996 cover. But her version is the blueprint.

"The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" is almost five minutes of patience. It's slow, spare and completely hypnotic.

"Tonight, I Celebrate My Love," her 1983 duet with Peabo Bryson, is a quiet storm classic that has played at weddings and anniversaries for decades.

And that's before you get to "Feel Like Makin' Love," or her duets with Donny Hathaway, like "Where Is the Love" and "The Closer I Get to You."

## Why she matters

Roberta Flack proved that soul music could be soft and still be powerful. A lot of the R&B that came after her, from quiet storm radio to neo-soul, owes something to the space she made.

She died in February 2025, at 88, after living with ALS. Her songs are going to outlive all of us.

## Quick answers

What are Roberta Flack's most famous songs? "Killing Me Softly with His Song," "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face," "Feel Like Makin' Love," "Where Is the Love" and "The Closer I Get to You" with Donny Hathaway, and "Tonight, I Celebrate My Love" with Peabo Bryson.

Did Roberta Flack win Record of the Year twice? Yes. She was the first artist to win it two years in a row, for "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" in 1973 and "Killing Me Softly with His Song" in 1974.

Who sang "Killing Me Softly" first? Lori Lieberman recorded it first, in 1972, but Roberta Flack's 1973 version made it a classic.

When did Roberta Flack die? On February 24, 2025, at age 88.

title: Honoring Michelle Trachtenberg | 4 Scenes Tribute
summary: Four scenes that defined Michelle Trachtenberg's career, packed into one minute: Harriet the Spy, Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Mysterious Skin and Gossip Girl. A tribute to a performer gone far too soon.
body:
Michelle Trachtenberg was one of those actors who seemed to grow up right alongside us. One minute she was the kid with the notebook in Harriet the Spy. The next, she was Buffy's little sister. Then she was Georgina Sparks, stealing every scene she walked into on Gossip Girl.

She died in February 2025, at just 39. So I put four moments that define her career into one minute, from kid star to scene-stealer.

## 1. Harriet the Spy (1996)

This is where a lot of us met her. Trachtenberg played Harriet M. Welsch, the 11-year-old who writes down everything she sees about everybody in her notebook, right up until her classmates find it.

The moment I picked is Harriet with her nanny, Ole Golly. When Golly tells her she's leaving, Harriet asks if she's going to be some other kid's nanny now, and love them more. Golly's answer, that there will only ever be one Harriet, still gets me. Trachtenberg was about 10 years old, and she carried a whole movie.

## 2. Buffy the Vampire Slayer (2000–2003)

In Season 5, Buffy suddenly has a little sister, Dawn, and the show makes you believe she's always been there. It turns out Dawn is the Key, mystical energy made human, and Trachtenberg had to play a teenager finding out she isn't "real."

The scene I used is from the Season 5 finale, "The Gift": the blood, the portal, Dawn begging Buffy to let her go, and Buffy's goodbye. "I love you. I will always love you." It's one of the most emotional moments in the whole series, and she's right in the middle of it.

## 3. Mysterious Skin (2004)

This is the one a lot of casual fans have never seen. Gregg Araki's Mysterious Skin is a dark, difficult movie, and Trachtenberg plays Wendy, the close friend of Joseph Gordon-Levitt's character, Neil. "I was infatuated with him too once. But I know all Neil's secrets."

It's a quieter role, and it proved she could do serious drama, far from the Nickelodeon-kid image she started with.

## 4. Gossip Girl (2008–2012)

And then there's Georgina Sparks. "Georgina Sparks. You know who I am."

Georgina was chaos in designer clothes: manipulative, unpredictable and seriously funny. You could tell Trachtenberg was having the time of her life playing her, and a character who could have been a one-off turned into one of the show's most memorable villains.

## Why these four

Put them side by side and you can see her whole range: a kid who could carry a movie, a teen who held her own on one of TV's best shows, a serious dramatic actor, and a villain everybody loved to hate.

She had plenty more, too: Inspector Gadget, EuroTrip, Ice Princess, 17 Again. But these four are the ones I'd show anybody who asks who she was.

## Quick answers

When did Michelle Trachtenberg die? On February 26, 2025, in New York City, at age 39.

Who did Michelle Trachtenberg play in Buffy the Vampire Slayer? Dawn Summers, Buffy's younger sister, from Season 5 through the end of the series.

Who did Michelle Trachtenberg play in Gossip Girl? Georgina Sparks, the scheming troublemaker.

What was Michelle Trachtenberg's first big movie role? The title role in Harriet the Spy (1996).

title: Chuck Norris: A Tribute to the Only Man Who Can Kick the Sun into the Sunset 🦅👊
summary: A tribute to Chuck Norris, the only man who can kick the sun into the sunset. From fighting Bruce Lee in Rome to protecting Texas as Walker, he was the ultimate symbol of justice. What was the first Chuck Norris movie you saw?
body:
Whether he was fighting in Rome or protecting the Texas border, Chuck Norris was the ultimate symbol of justice. He's also the only man who can kick the sun into the sunset. Those are just facts.

Chuck Norris died on March 19, 2026, at 86. So this one is a tribute to a legend: a real martial artist, a real action star, and the only man who became an internet meme without even trying.

## The fighter before the movies

Before Hollywood, Norris was the real deal. He started training in martial arts while serving in the U.S. Air Force in South Korea, became a world karate champion and went on to create his own style, Chun Kuk Do. When he threw a kick on screen, you knew he could throw it for real.

## Fighting Bruce Lee in the Colosseum

In 1972's The Way of the Dragon, Norris faced Bruce Lee in Rome's Colosseum. It's one of the most famous fight scenes ever filmed: two real martial artists, no tricks, in a building made for gladiators. Norris lost the fight, but he walked out of that movie a star.

## The '80s action run

In the '80s, Norris was a one-man action franchise. Missing in Action. Code of Silence. Invasion U.S.A. The Delta Force. If you grew up with a VCR, there's a good chance a Chuck Norris tape was sitting on the shelf.

## Walker, Texas Ranger

Then came Cordell Walker. Walker, Texas Ranger ran on CBS from 1993 to 2001 and made Norris a Saturday-night staple for a whole generation. Bad guys, roundhouse kicks and a lesson at the end. That's the Chuck Norris a lot of us grew up with.

## The Expendables 2 and the cobra

By 2012, the internet had already turned him into a legend with "Chuck Norris facts." So in The Expendables 2, he got to play right into it. His character, Booker, is asked about a rumor that he was bitten by a king cobra. His answer: yes, and after five days of agonizing pain, the cobra died.

Nothing sums up Chuck Norris better, except maybe a roundhouse kick.

## Why he mattered

Chuck Norris went from real champion to movie star to TV icon to meme, and he stayed Chuck Norris the whole way through: tough, calm and on the side of the good guys.

Rest easy, Walker.

## Quick answers

When did Chuck Norris die? On March 19, 2026, at age 86, after a medical emergency in Hawaii.

Did Chuck Norris fight Bruce Lee? Yes, on screen. Their fight in Rome's Colosseum is the climax of The Way of the Dragon (1972).

How long did Walker, Texas Ranger run? Eight seasons, from 1993 to 2001, on CBS.

What's the Chuck Norris cobra joke? In The Expendables 2, his character says he was bitten by a king cobra and, after five days of agonizing pain, the cobra died.

title: Young Martin: They Are Turning This 90s Comedy Into a Gritty Modern Drama
summary: They're turning Martin into Young Martin, an hour-long gritty drama set in modern-day Detroit. How do you take the peak physical comedy of the '90s and make it serious? Plus the Martin spin-off that got it right: The Varnell Hill Show.
body:
I couldn't believe this was real. They're doing a Young Martin prequel, and here's the catch: they're turning it into an hour-long, gritty drama set in modern-day Detroit.

How do you take the peak physical comedy of the '90s and turn it into a serious drama?

## Martin was physical comedy at its peak

Martin ran on Fox from 1992 to 1997, and it was Martin Lawrence at full power. He didn't just play Martin Payne. He also played Sheneneh, Jerome, Mama Payne, Otis the security guard and more, sometimes several of them in the same episode.

The show ran on energy: the falls, the faces, the timing and a studio audience losing it. Martin, Gina, Tommy, Pam and Cole felt like family, and the laugh track was part of the fun. Martin Lawrence's energy had so much soul, and you can't separate it from the format.

## What Young Martin is supposed to be

Young Martin was announced in July 2024, with Martin Lawrence producing. It follows a teenage Martin Payne in present-day Detroit, and it's pitched as an hour-long drama about family, friendship and growing up, built around a teenager "characterized by ambition, humor, and a genuine compassion for those around him."

If that sounds familiar, it's because it's the Bel-Air playbook: take a beloved '90s sitcom and re-imagine it as a serious, cinematic drama.

## Why the gritty remake keeps missing the point

Bel-Air did it to The Fresh Prince. It changed the tone, the theme and the whole point of the show, and turned a comedy into a prestige drama.

I get why studios do it. The name brings the nostalgia, and drama feels more "premium." But it uses the nostalgia while throwing away the reason people are nostalgic in the first place. Martin worked because it was genuinely funny, loud and silly, with real heart underneath. Take the comedy out, and all that's left is the name.

Modern TV wants to make everything dark and sterile. Not everything needs to be.

## Update (September 2026): The Varnell Hill Show got it right

Here's the good news. There's a new Martin spin-off, and it's the opposite of Young Martin.

The Varnell Hill Show premiered on Paramount+ on September 1. Tommy Davidson is back as Varnell Hill, Martin's old rival, in a workplace comedy set behind the scenes of a long-running late-night talk show, where Varnell is fighting to stay relevant in a fast-changing entertainment world. Martin Lawrence has a recurring role, and the cast includes Kym Whitley, Wendy Raquel Robinson, Nick Cafero, Emmanuel Hudson and Chris Williams, with guest stars like Damon Wayans, Mike Epps, Deon Cole, Ms. Pat and Omarion. The eight-episode first season runs weekly through October 13.

And I love it. It's got the laugh track, just like back in the day. They didn't go the modern, cinematic route, and they didn't change what the show is about, the way they did when The Fresh Prince became Bel-Air. It feels like Martin's world, and that's exactly how it should feel.

As for Young Martin, I haven't seen a network or a premiere date announced yet.

Sources: [Deadline](https://deadline.com/2026/08/the-varnell-hill-show-premiere-date-paramount-plus-photos-1237018677/), [The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/martin-spinoff-varnell-hill-show-premiere-1236665164/), [Variety](https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/martin-spinoff-varnell-hill-show-release-date-1236828346/), [Deadline on Young Martin](https://deadline.com/2024/07/martin-prequel-drama-series-martin-lawrence-marvin-peart-1236007272/)

## Quick answers

What is The Varnell Hill Show? A Martin spin-off comedy on Paramount+, starring Tommy Davidson as Varnell Hill and set behind the scenes of a late-night talk show. It premiered September 1, 2026.

Is Martin Lawrence in The Varnell Hill Show? Yes, in a recurring role.

What is Young Martin? A planned hour-long drama prequel about a teenage Martin Payne in present-day Detroit, announced in 2024. It doesn't have a network or premiere date yet.

When did Martin air? On Fox, from 1992 to 1997.

title: Original Barney vs. CGI Barney: Why 90s Practical Effects Still Hit Harder Than CGI
summary: The original Barney was a real costume, and it felt real. The new CGI Barney feels cold and sterile by comparison. Did we lose the magic of practical effects, or is it just the nostalgia talking?
body:
There's something about the practical effects and the physical suit from the '90s that made the original Barney feel real. The new 3D animated Barney just feels cold and sterile.

I know, I know. It's Barney. But hear me out, because this is the whole practical-effects-versus-CGI argument in its purest form.

## The original Barney was in the room

Barney & Friends started on PBS in 1992, and Barney was a real costume: a performer inside a big purple dinosaur suit, with another performer doing the voice, on a real set with real kids.

That's why he felt real. When Barney hugged somebody, a body was hugging them. When he danced, the suit moved, squished and wobbled like something that actually existed. The kids on set were reacting to something that was really there, and you could feel it through the screen.

## The new Barney is a render

In 2024, Mattel brought Barney back with Barney's World, the first Barney series that's fully animated. It premiered on Max and Cartoon Network in October 2024, and the redesign started arguments as soon as people saw it.

From a pure character design perspective, it feels like we traded the soul of handmade TV for a cheap digital render. Everything is smooth, clean and perfectly lit, and none of it has any weight. He's not sharing a room with anybody. He's sharing a file.

I'm not the only one who felt that way, either. People from the original show spoke out against the change, including Jessica Zucha, who played Tina, and Dianna De La Garza, who played Angela.

## Why practical still hits harder

This isn't just a Barney thing. It's the same reason people still bring up The Thing, the animatronic dinosaurs in Jurassic Park and the Deadites in Evil Dead:

- A physical thing has weight. Light hits it the same way it hits everything else in the scene.
- Actors react to something that's really there, so their reactions are real.
- Little imperfections, like a seam, a wobble or a weird shadow, make it feel alive instead of manufactured.

CGI can do things practical effects never could. But when a character is supposed to feel like a friend in the room with you, a suit on a set beats a render almost every time.

## To be fair to the new show

Kids today don't care about any of this. Barney's World ranked among the top five kids' shows on Max after it launched, so the new Barney is clearly working for the audience it's made for. This is a grown-up complaint from people who grew up with the old one.

But that's exactly the question.

## Quick answers

title: The Numbers Don't Lie: Nintendo's Evolution from Couch Co-op to the Switch Era
summary: From '90s and 2000s couch co-op to the Switch 2's fast start, I tracked Nintendo's console sales era by era. Which Nintendo generation defined your childhood?
body:
The numbers don't lie. 📊

I tracked Nintendo's evolution from the golden era of '90s and 2000s couch co-op to the modern juggernauts of the Switch generation. When I posted this, the original Switch had passed 155 million units, and the Switch 2 was already out of the gate with nearly 20 million sold.

Here's how every Nintendo home console stacks up.

## The home console scoreboard

Lifetime units sold worldwide, from Nintendo's own figures:

- NES (1983): 61.91 million
- Super Nintendo (1990): 49.10 million
- Nintendo 64 (1996): 32.93 million
- GameCube (2001): 21.74 million
- Wii (2006): 101.63 million
- Wii U (2012): 13.56 million
- Switch (2017): 156.59 million and counting
- Switch 2 (2025): 23.68 million and counting

Years are the original Japanese launches, and the Switch numbers are as of June 30, 2026.

## The couch co-op era

The N64 and GameCube never sold like the NES or the Wii, but ask anybody who grew up with them: four controller ports changed everything. GoldenEye, Mario Kart 64, Mario Party, Super Smash Bros. Melee, Double Dash: that era was built around everybody in the same room, yelling at the same screen.

Then the Wii took that idea to the whole family and sold more than 100 million consoles doing it.

## The Wii U stumble and the Switch comeback

The Wii U is the reminder that Nintendo can miss. At 13.56 million, it's Nintendo's lowest-selling home console. But the Switch answered it by combining home console and handheld, and it became Nintendo's best-selling console ever, passing the Nintendo DS's 154.02 million.

## The Switch 2 is moving fast

The Switch 2 launched in June 2025 and passed the GameCube's entire lifetime total in about 13 months. Nintendo expects to sell 16.5 million more this fiscal year.

## Update (September 2026)

As of June 30, 2026, Nintendo reported 23.68 million Switch 2 units and 156.59 million for the original Switch. The Switch 2's U.S. price also went up on September 1, from $449.99 to $499.99.

Sources: [Nintendo Life](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2026/08/switch-2-surpasses-23-million-units-as-nintendo-claims-sales-remain-solid), [VGChartz](https://www.vgchartz.com/article/468666/switch-2-ships-2368-million-units-as-of-june-2026-switch-1-ships-15659-million/), [Variety](https://variety.com/2026/gaming/news/nintendo-switch-2-price-increase-20-million-sold-1236741441/)

## Quick answers

What is Nintendo's best-selling console? The Nintendo Switch, with 156.59 million units as of June 30, 2026.

How many Switch 2 consoles have been sold? 23.68 million as of June 30, 2026.

How many Wii consoles were sold? 101.63 million.

What is Nintendo's worst-selling home console? The Wii U, at 13.56 million, not counting the Virtual Boy.

title: PBS Kids — POV: You forgot these defined your childhood 📼 #nostalgia #90skids #shorts
summary: The nostalgia hit me like a truck. From Wishbone to Ghostwriter, these PBS Kids shows raised a whole generation. Which one did you run home from school to watch?
body:
The nostalgia just hit me like a truck.

This short is a montage of PBS Kids shows from back in the day, the ones a lot of us used to run home from school to watch, from Wishbone to Ghostwriter. We forget how much these shows shaped us. They were teaching us to read, solve problems and get curious, and we thought we were just watching TV.

## Wishbone

A Jack Russell terrier who imagined himself as the hero of classic books. In every episode of Wishbone, something in his everyday life reminded him of a story, and suddenly he was Sherlock Holmes, Robin Hood or a character from Shakespeare. In costume. As a dog.

It sounds ridiculous, and it was. It also got a lot of kids to read Oliver Twist and The Odyssey without realizing they were doing homework.

## Ghostwriter

Ghostwriter was a mystery show about a group of kids in Brooklyn who solved cases with help from a ghost nobody could see or hear. The only way the ghost could communicate was by moving letters and words around: on signs, on computer screens, in books.

So the whole show was secretly about reading and writing. And it worked, because it was genuinely tense and fun. The team, the pens on necklaces, the "Rally!" messages: if you know, you know. It even got a reboot on Apple TV+ in 2019.

## The rest of the lineup

Those two weren't alone. That era of PBS was stacked: Arthur, The Magic School Bus, Reading Rainbow, Bill Nye the Science Guy, Zoom, and Barney for the little ones. The PBS Kids brand itself launched in 1999, but for a lot of us, the golden age was already well underway.

## Why these shows hit different

These shows weren't trying to keep you watching. They were trying to send you somewhere else: to the library, to a book, outside to try an experiment. No algorithm, no autoplay. Just a show, then the next show, then dinner.

That's probably why they stick with us. They weren't content. They were part of growing up.

## Quick answers

What was Wishbone about? A Jack Russell terrier who imagined himself as characters from classic literature, like Sherlock Holmes and Robin Hood. It aired on PBS in the '90s.

What was Ghostwriter about? A group of Brooklyn kids who solved mysteries with help from a ghost who could only communicate by rearranging written words.

When did Ghostwriter first air? On PBS, starting in 1992.

What shows were on PBS for kids in the '90s? Favorites included Wishbone, Ghostwriter, Arthur, The Magic School Bus, Reading Rainbow, Bill Nye the Science Guy and Barney & Friends.

## Your turn

Which PBS Kids show was your favorite, and who did you use to watch it with? Tell me in the comments.

Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods are two-thirds of The New Day, one of the most decorated tag teams in WWE history, and they left together. Releases usually hit random names from different corners of the roster. This one took out whole units: a legendary tag team and half of an active faction. And it came in a year when WWE has already let go of dozens of wrestlers, including former world champions like Sheamus.

When the cuts start hitting connected groups instead of individuals, that tells you the company is reshaping entire parts of the show, not just trimming the roster.
